cases.assessment: Wilson1894 has the complete continuous prayer. Its same-edition apparatus independently records ministerio, so that reading is not simply a modern invented change. Target meritis differs from the old merito by number/case inflection in the existing et ... et numero construction. Read together with the recorded comma/pointing and actual Per Dominum stop, the contribution introduces no new petition, clause or nontrivial expressive arrangement. A qualified insufficient-originality basis is defensible for this exact whole body. This is not a claim that the main text itself prints the entire target sequence.
cases.strongest_counterargument: The choice of plural merits may express deliberate theological redaction, and a critical text plus apparatus is not an already printed full target sequence. A low originality threshold requires considering the combined selection, not automatically exempting a short grammatical change. Here one reading is explicitly old and the remaining inflection is conventional within an otherwise unchanged complete source prayer; the limited expressive contribution supports policy1(6), with that uncertainty retained.

cases.whole_contribution_assessment: Use the complete same-feast1922 Offertory as the historical foundation, already including the final Alleluia. The only later lexical addition is omnibus before insidiis, a conventional universal quantifier in the same preserved complete prayer. It extends the expressed scope and is not erased as spelling. In the exact unchanged old syntax this one ordinary quantifier adds insufficient independently creative expression to defeat the old foundation. The separate Passion version is corroborating contrary evidence, not a second donor spliced into an asserted old whole.
cases.strongest_counterargument_and_limit: Direct1922 and1862 feast bodies omit omnibus; the Passion body includes it but lacks the final acclamation. No exact pre1931 full selected target utterance or first-publication date is established. Semantic broadening can be deliberate and the whole combined expression matters; the recommendation rests on the complete feast source plus the limited ordinary quantifier, not on merging distinct source utterances or a universal short-word exemption.

shared_policy_assessment: Apply liturgical-text-publication-policy section1(6) as a qualified finite project judgment, not a blanket copyright clearance or an assertion that every old phrase can be assembled into a free modern prayer.

Each candidate has a complete continuous independently established old underlying expression. Its whole measured contribution is assessed in context: old-attested grammatical form/one inflection, one quantifier, or a standard final seasonal invocation with actual source-owned condition. No unrelated old fragments are stitched into a claimed historical whole.

The CopyrightOffice individual-word/short-expression and derivative-work originality principles support a defensible limited-contribution argument, while their low creativity threshold and possible originality of selection/arrangement remain explicit. Semantic significance alone is not equivalent to protectable added expression, but shortness alone is not immunity either.
